messages:
kevin: thinking out loud — proposal to move dashboard panel rendering to a streaming projection service that emits precomputed panel frames + pre-signed RBAC tokens for render-time checks
anya: can you sketch the shape? streaming projection = background job that materializes panel payloads? how do RBAC tokens fit in?
devon: curious about complexity. we already have the query service + auth middleware. why add another surface area?
kevin: short version — split responsibilities: query service stays authoritative for fresh reads, projection service keeps frequently-read panel state (tiling/aggregates) and issues ephemeral tokens that encode allowed viewer scopes so the console client can do cheap checks without roundtrips. goal: shave tail latency and reduce fanout at render time.
marta: big tradeoff is revocation. if a user's permission is removed, pre-signed token could still allow renders until expiry. what's the TTL model?
kevin: yes — TTL + write-side invalidation. tokens default to 30s, but we can force immediate invalidation for critical security events by bubbling an invalidation event to projection service which marks tokens revoked and starts rejecting. still, there's a small window.
anya: 30s seems fine for most dashboards, but some cross-tenant admin actions might need instant effect. we should classify panels: sensitive vs non-sensitive. sensitive panels always hit query service sync. non-sensitive can use projection + token.
devon: fallback plan? if projection service is down, dashboards must still render.
kevin: fallback -> client switches to legacy path (query service) based on feature flag/route. projection exposes health endpoint and we gate routing in the routing layer. also circuit-breaker that sends traffic back to query service automatically.
marta: what about cache churn and mem pressure? projection will hold a lot of windowed aggregates. need eviction strategy + metrics. also quantify cost delta vs current ops.
kevin: agreed — plan includes cost model and a perf budget. initial pilot will be 5 panels across 10% of tenants, measure: p99 render latency, request fanout, queries/sec, infra cost.
anya: rollout config proposal?
kevin: sketch:
```
pilot:
  percent_tenants: 10
  panels: [usage_summary, recent_activities, top_alerts, token_chart, ingest_rate]
token:
  ttl_seconds: 30
  revocation_stream: enabled
health:
  fallback_threshold: 5%  # error rate to trigger fallback
```
devon: add test plan: synthetic load with permission flips (revoke/grant) at scale, and probe for token misuse. also smoke test for stale data windows.
kevin: yep — test plan includes: loadtest w/ revokes, chaos on projection nodes, failover to query path, and A/B UX sampling for perceived latency.
sre-bot: loadtest results from staging yesterday: projection prototype at 25% traffic reduced median render by 180ms, p99 by 340ms, and backend fanout by ~42%.
marta: nice. want to make sure we have RBAC correctness checks in CI — fuzz permission combinations and assert no leakage.
anya: also add observability: token issuance rate, token revocation latency, projection freshness lag, panel miss rate.
kevin: volunteers for migration spike? i'll own orchestration and rollout gates. devon and marta?
devon: in. can take the loadtesting + fallback hooks.
marta: in. i'll own RBAC test harness and metrics.
kevin: thanks — I'll write the RFC follow-up with diagram + cost numbers and send a canary checklist. plan to kickoff spike next week. :rocket:
deploy-bot: deploy queued: projection-prototype -> staging at 2025-03-11T16:12:08Z :hourglass_flowing_sand:
kevin: ping when staging perf is stable, then we can schedule the pilot. :+1:
